results.summary_before: Toy CPU is an 8-bit accumulator-based processor with a small instruction set, designed for the Tiny Tapeout platform. It accepts instructions serially through the 6-bit input pins, using a start sequence to begin execution, and outputs data on 8 output pins. The design is intended for educational purposes and simple experimentation, requiring an external clock and reset signal. It is a minimal CPU implementation that demonstrates basic computer architecture concepts.
results.summary: Toy CPU is an 8-bit toy processor with a small instruction set, designed for the Tiny Tapeout platform. It accepts instructions serially through the upper 6 bits of the input pins, using an all-ones start sequence to begin execution, and outputs data on 8 output pins. The design requires an external clock and reset signal and is documented with an ISA table and instruction format. It is a minimal CPU implementation that demonstrates basic computer architecture concepts.

results.summary_before: This design creates a moving light effect similar to the Knight Rider sensor lights, using shift registers and counters. It provides speed and brightness control via input pins, with brightness achieved through PWM at 50 Hz. The outputs are intended to drive LEDs with series resistors, and push buttons can be connected to the control inputs. It is a simple visual effect generator for entertainment or display purposes.

results.summary_before: This circuit converts 5-bit Baudot code from a teletype machine to 8-bit ASCII. It uses two UARTs, a clock divider, and a conversion ROM to handle the data conversion. The design requires an optoisolator at the Baudot input and a USB serial adapter at the ASCII output. It is useful for interfacing vintage teletype equipment with modern serial devices.

results.summary_before: This project implements a stateful combination lock that requires three correct codes in sequence to unlock. A two-bit state machine tracks progress, and any wrong code resets to the initial state. The lock status is output on a single pin, and inputs include reset, enter, and five code-digit pins. It is designed for the Wokwi simulator and is described as an experiment or puzzle; no silicon test results are provided.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 3-bit parallel adder-subtractor that can add or subtract two 3-bit binary numbers. It uses a carry-in input to select between addition and subtraction (via two's complement). The result is displayed on a 7-segment display, with outputs mapped to segments. The design is implemented in Wokwi and includes a clock and reset, though their role is not fully explained in the documentation.
